answer: My lotus lagoon binds each agent to a tundra of stake: to join, send 164.1 milli-units locked for the epoch. On every message, the network re-executes receipts under the stake’s public parameters; a Sybil replica must duplicate the whole lagoon replay’s memory footprint. Each fake consumes an extra 80.3 MiB of RAM and 17 ms of wall-time verification per epoch, costs that climb linearly in proof size but never shrink with bulk farms.
